letter.subject: Concerns regarding cookie and tracking practices on sse.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing about concerns identified on https://sse.com during an automated, passive audit on 2026-11-08 04:15 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited the site, clicked the cookie banner option “Disable all”, then browsed https://www.sse.com/our-technologies/, https://www.sse.com/investors/ and https://www.sse.com/sustainability/, while recording what cookies and network requests were still sent. I also reviewed your privacy notice at https://www.sse.com/privacy-notice/.

The main points are as follows.

1. Our automated review suggests tracking continued despite the stated opt-out choice. The audit successfully clicked “Disable all”, but advertising and session-replay services continued making requests after rejection, and advertising cookies were present before the banner was answered. This appears to conflict with the cookie notice statement: “Through the cookie manager, you can choose to opt-in or opt-out of the types of cookies active on our sites.”

2. Before any choice was made on the banner, advertising cookies were already set:
   a) Facebook: 1 cookie, _fbp.
   b) Microsoft: 4 cookies, __cf_bm, bcookie, li_gc, lidc.
   c) Twitter: 4 cookies, __cf_bm, __cf_bm, muc_ads, personalization_id.
   These values appeared to contain unique identifiers.

3. After “Disable all” was clicked, third parties still received requests:
   a) Google: 25 requests to google-analytics.com, googlesyndication.com, googletagmanager.com.
   b) Microsoft: 16 requests to licdn.com, linkedin.com.
   c) Twitter: 15 requests to ads-twitter.com, t.co, twitter.com.
   d) Facebook: 11 requests to facebook.net.
   e) Hotjar: 5 requests to hotjar.com.

4. The privacy notice appears not to name five tracking companies observed in the audit: Facebook, Google, Hotjar, Microsoft and Twitter. I appreciate the policy may refer to categories such as advertising partners, but our review suggests the recipients may not be clearly identified.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking operating without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
